rationale.automation-bias: Experienced developers self-report secure-coding proficiency erosion when using GAI.
rationale.quality-debt: Participants report harder code comprehension and greater documentation needs.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Developers report using scanners and tests on generated code.
rationale.hitl-workflow: Practitioners manually review generated code before integration and production.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Documentation and code understanding support human security judgments.
rationale.survey-input: Survey quantifies adoption, trust, practices, and organizational security priorities.
rationale.assistive: Study covers completion tools accepted within human-led coding.
rationale.agentic: Study explicitly compares full-program generation against code completion.
rationale.non-developer: About half the sample were students, hobbyists, freelancers, or nonprofessionals.
rationale.risk-security: Survey reports vulnerability concerns, confidence, and security-review behavior.
rationale.risk-quality: Code comprehensibility and maintainability receive substantive empirical treatment.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Sixty-five percent identify overreliance without human oversight as greatest risk.
rationale.risk-bias: Fifty-six percent identify future bias in generated code as challenging.
rationale.method-self-report: Questionnaire gathers developers’ reported perceptions, behaviors, and practices.
